subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<skillKey>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec deny boundary for that skill directory, or should OpenClaw keep it prompt-only and add a separate strict skill-access policy?
rationale: Both options change operator expectations: hard denial improves safety but can be a compatibility break, while a separate strict mode preserves current behavior but leaves the reported security gap unless operators opt in.

options.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard boundary
options.body: Treat disabled skill directories as denied roots everywhere the agent can read, write, materialize, or execute skill files, with docs and upgrade notes for the behavior change.

options.title: Add an explicit strict skill-access policy
options.body: Keep current `enabled:false` prompt semantics and add a separate operator-controlled enforcement mode for deployments that require a hard skill filesystem boundary.

options.title: Document prompt-only semantics
options.body: Declare disabled skills as prompt/eligibility-only and rely on sandbox, tool policy, install policy, and OS isolation for hard security boundaries.

recommendation.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat disabled skill directories as denied roots everywhere the agent can read, write, materialize, or execute skill files, with docs and upgrade notes for the behavior change.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses secops-owned agent/sandbox paths and Peter has recent security and exec-policy history in the affected area.
